title: Defections and unstable State governments after 1967
body: After the fourth general elections of February 1967, the Congress lost power in nine States. In many of them, coalition governments of non-Congress parties were formed, often by partners with very different ideologies. Defection, in which an elected representative leaves the party on whose symbol he or she was elected and joins another party, now played an important role. Breakaway Congress legislators helped to install non-Congress governments in Haryana, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh. In Haryana, an MLA named Gaya Lal changed his party three times within a fortnight, which gave rise to the phrase 'Aya Ram, Gaya Ram'. Most of the non-Congress coalition governments did not last long: they lost their majority, and either new combinations were formed or President's rule had to be imposed. Later, the Constitution was amended to prevent defections.

title: The verdict of 1971
body: In the fifth Lok Sabha elections held in February 1971, Indira Gandhi's Congress(R) contested in alliance with the Communist Party of India (CPI). Opposing them was the Grand Alliance of the SSP, PSP, Bharatiya Jana Sangh, Swatantra Party and Bharatiya Kranti Dal, along with the Congress(O). The Congress(R)-CPI combine won 375 seats and secured 48.4 per cent of the votes. On its own, the Congress(R) won 352 seats with about 44 per cent of the popular votes. The Congress(O), the party with so many stalwarts, got less than one-fourth of the votes of Indira Gandhi's party and won merely 16 seats. The combined tally of the Grand Alliance was less than 60 seats.
